lessons_learned.observation: The redesign catalyst failed to overcome rotation pressure once volume confirmation lagged
lessons_learned.adjustment: Require volume above the 20-day average before entering any catalyst-driven name already in a sector rotation

lessons_learned.observation: The modest gain validated the earnings catalyst but also showed how single-name fintech exposure can lag broader tech rotation even on positive news
lessons_learned.adjustment: Always cross-check sector rotation signals before sizing earnings-driven entries

lessons_learned.observation: Without closing prices we cannot measure whether the leadership-change catalyst produced any excess return relative to the broader market
lessons_learned.adjustment: Require closing-price confirmation before declaring any catalyst trade complete

lessons_learned.observation: The launch catalyst produced no sustained follow-through once broader market volatility from geopolitical headlines took over
lessons_learned.adjustment: Require both a fundamental catalyst and a volume spike above the 20-day average before committing capital to healthcare launches

lessons_learned.observation: The valuation setup delivered modest stability on a down day for growth indices, showing that depressed multiples can act as a buffer when momentum names rotate
lessons_learned.adjustment: Pair valuation screens with a same-day volume check before treating any rebound as confirmed

lessons_learned.observation: The earnings-driven momentum entry worked because data-center demand exceeded expectations and sector rotation supported the move
lessons_learned.adjustment: Always require volume confirmation above the 20-day average before entering momentum trades on earnings beats

lessons_learned.observation: Capturing a modest same-day gain validated quick execution on cross-asset signals, yet the portfolio’s persistent underperformance versus the NASDAQ underscores how difficult it remains to generate consistent alpha with single-day volatile assets
lessons_learned.adjustment: Always cross-check crypto price feeds with at least two independent sources before executing flash trades

lessons_learned.observation: Capturing a modest gain on the BTC flash trade validated the use of cross-asset signals for opportunistic entries, but the underperformance relative to the NASDAQ underscores the difficulty of beating broad indices on single-day volatile assets. The key adjustment is strengthening confirmation criteria to ensure the signal has substance beyond initial movement
lessons_learned.adjustment: Always verify price data from multiple providers before entering a flash trade on volatile assets like crypto

lessons_learned.observation: The bid-ask-spread / order-flow-slippage lesson was taught in 6 of 8 recent episodes with nearly identical framing. Listeners tuned out after the third repeat.
lessons_learned.adjustment: Never re-teach bid_ask_spread or order_flow_slippage within their 45-day cooldown. If the only interesting mechanic today is a stale one, pick a different mechanic — freshness beats any single lesson.

lessons_learned.observation: The last 10 picks skewed 35% toward precious metals (Fortuna, SSR, West Red Lake) with zero flag raised on air. A real portfolio would have rebalanced.
lessons_learned.adjustment: Cap any single sector at 30% of the trailing 10-trade window. When the sector-concentration warning fires, the Practice Investment MUST pick a different sector that episode.

rows.name: hold
rows.story: growth stops today; the factory keeps publishing

assumptions: Scenarios, not forecasts — none of this is booked revenue.
Revenue capacity = monthly downloads × 12 ÷ 1,000 × CPM × slots (low: 1 programmatic slot at $12 CPM; high: 2 host-read slots at $50 CPM). The network currently sells zero ads.
Implied EV applies the 1–4x revenue multiple observed across 2020-24 podcast M&A to that capacity IF it were realized.
Episode counts assume the current cadence (~86/week) simply continues — the factory's marginal cost makes that the default, not a stretch.
Library replacement value prices episodes at boutique production rates ($200–$400). It is a cost-basis framing, not a resale price.
Trailing reality check: median WoW download growth over recent weeks is 4.7% — the scenarios deliberately assume much less.

channel_scorecard.window_note: WoW = last 7 COMPLETE analytics days vs the 7 before (the trailing 2 days are excluded as unreported lag), anchored to the analytics fetch. zero_view_share compares INDEX uploads with analytics rows over the same lag-trimmed window — the API omits zero-activity videos, so this is the FR-launch early warning.

experiments.title: Shorts progress bar (all channels)
experiments.target: Short median AVP up vs the ~44% pre-bar level (compare EN+RU short retention before/after 08-07 in youtube_stats).
experiments.notes: Thin animated cyan bar at the top of every Short — visible time remaining, the standard short-video retention device. Render-only; per-show opt-out youtube.shorts_progress_bar: false. NOTE: overlaps the staggered-shorts readout window — judge by retention (AVP), which stagger does not touch, not by views.

experiments.title: Site-showcase endings — outro card + Shorts site strip
experiments.target: utm_content=outro sessions appearing in api/funnel.json (QR scans) and click-through from video surfaces up vs the pre-08-09 level; newsletter captures from src-youtube-* tags are the end goal.
experiments.notes: Long-form videos end on a card built from real nerranetwork.com screenshots (show page + network home) with a QR to the funnel-tagged show page; Shorts end cards gain the home page's show-grid strip. Render-only (outside landmine #17); per-show opt-outs youtube.outro_card_enabled / youtube.shorts_end_card_site_panel. Screenshots are committed (assets/site_screens) and refreshed by scripts/capture_site_screens.py.

experiments.title: @NerraFR — keep or pause the dub channel
experiments.criteria: Keep if any FR show reaches short_vpd >= 1.0 or organic subscriber traction appears by 2026-08-25; else pause FR dubs (youtube.dub_languages: [] on the four shows — one line, reversible). FR PODCAST tracks are decided separately via the per-language OP3 instrument.
experiments.notes: 53 of 72 launch-window uploads had zero recorded views. Clean analytics only since 2026-07-29 (the glob fix), hence the late decision date rather than a same-day verdict.

experiments.title: Seek-bar chapters ship in every long-form description
experiments.target: Long-form median AVP up vs the 13.4% (14d) baseline, and chapter-driven "Key moments" appearing in search — chapters had NEVER shipped (0 of 1,333 committed chapter files started at 0:00, so the formatter discarded every block).
experiments.notes: Synthetic localized "0:00 Intro" line prepended when chapter 1 starts after the music intro (clamped when it starts <10s). Metadata-only — outside landmine #17. Confounded with the caption-hold + end-card caption fixes shipping the same day; read AVP as the joint effect of the retention batch.

experiments.title: Shorts captions hold through pauses + stay visible over the end card
experiments.target: Shorts median averageViewPercentage up vs the 50.8% EN / 43.6% RU (14d) baselines; specifically less drop-off in the final 3 s (end-card window) once retention curves are fetched.
experiments.notes: Per-word ASS cues extend to the next word's start (card no longer flickers off 10-20x per Short at breaths) and the subtitles stage runs after the end-card overlay (last ~3 s of speech kept its text hidden under the opaque CTA card). Render-only — outside landmine #17.

experiments.title: Long-form scene cadence — input dedup + 36-slot cap + adaptive Ken Burns
experiments.target: Long-form median AVP up vs the 13.4%/11.4% (14d) recent band. A 17-min episode now changes scene every ~29 s instead of holding 85+ s, the accelerating open survives, and Ken Burns speed no longer collapses on long holds (0.006/s adaptive amplitude). Reads jointly with youtube-chapters-live (both target the same metric; this is the render half).
experiments.notes: Enabled by ffmpeg input dedup (one -i per unique image + split), which removed the per-slot demuxer cost behind the old 24-slot cap. Render-only — outside landmine #17.

experiments.title: Modern Investing states verified-window alpha only
experiments.baseline: +9.28% across 45 trades spoken on air; the 10 honestly-measured trades were at -1.95%
experiments.target: Every alpha figure spoken on air comes from the 10 (and growing) trades with pick-date-aligned benchmark windows, with the trade count in the same sentence. No blended lifetime alpha reaches air.
experiments.criteria: OPERATOR DECISION at readout: run `scripts/recompute_mit_benchmarks.py --apply` (needs market-data access) to rebuild the 35 legacy windows. That collapses the split — every trade gains entry_bar_date and the verified figure simply becomes the whole record. Until it runs, the show's headline is honest but built on n=10.
experiments.notes: The recompute has been an open operator item in the MIT ledger since 2026-07-03. This change stops the unrun backfill from silently flattering the on-air number in the meantime.

experiments.title: Live search queries feed titles + tags
experiments.baseline: EN search share 15% of channel views (2026-08-17); terms: starship flight 14, fsd v14.1 lite, ...
experiments.target: EN YT_SEARCH share of views up vs 15%, and search terms appearing in shipped titles/tags. The Analytics search-terms report now flows per-show (token-matched, conservative) into youtube_performance.json — the title prompt gets a LIVE SEARCH QUERIES line and uploads prepend the matched terms as tags.
experiments.notes: Channel-level terms are attributed to a show only when they share a meaningful token with its recent titles/hooks; unmatched terms are dropped rather than sprayed across the channel. Metadata-only.

experiments.title: grok-4.6 staged trial — dp_pod script, synth, reviewer (FPD+UC arms withdrawn 2026-08-27)
experiments.baseline: All stages on grok-4.3 after the same-day revert of the network-wide 4.6 upgrade. dp_pod on 4.3: zero exclamation points in 27/30 episodes, Ep22 65% verbatim digest paste. FPD/UC: the accepted grok-4.3 narrative-length plateau (briefs 848-1116w vs 1600 ask). FPD/UC digest latency on 4.3: ~30-50s.
experiments.target: dp_pod scripts follow the delivery spec (exclamations/voice tags present, shingle overlap with the digest clearly below the 65%/42% worst cases). FPD/UC briefs come off the 4.3 plateau without the banned podcast-side retries. No latency regressions: stage durations in metrics_ep*.json stay under 50% of NERRA_LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (600s) and zero 'Slow LLM completion' warnings after week one.
experiments.criteria: Operator-directed staged rollout per docs/model_upgrade_playbook.md (the first trial run under it). SCOPE: dp_pod llm.podcast_model ONLY (digest stays 4.3); first_principles + unintended_consequences whole-show (narrative — the brief is model-knowledge prose); synth_model + reviewer_model in _defaults. Every daily NEWS show's digest/fetch stays grok-4.3. REVERT TRIGGERS, any one suffices, revert = delete the named pin: (1) an invented fact/date/name in an FPD or UC story (these are factual histories) — judged against the other shows' FACTUAL_ERRORS under the SAME 4.6 reviewer, never against pre-08-18 history (the reviewer instrument changed this date too); (2) a digest/script stage exceeding ~300s repeatedly or any request timeout on a trial show; (3) a missed episode attributable to the model; (4) dp_pod A/B-listen verdict against the 4.6 scripts (landmine #17 — prose changes with the model).
experiments.notes: Follow-up to network-grok-46-upgrade (reverted for latency, not quality — the quality question was never answered). Trial shows were picked benefit-over-risk: dp_pod's dialogue writing is its product and its 4.3 failures are documented writing-model limitations; FPD/UC have no news fetch so a stronger model is the only sanctioned length/depth lever; synth + reviewer are analysis-stage, operator-gated or non-published. The four biggest-prompt news shows (tesla, spacex, omni_view, MIT) stay OFF 4.6 — highest hallucination stakes and the four that timed out on outage day. NERRA_LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS raised 300 -> 600 in run-show.yml (worst-case per stage 3 x 600s = 30 min, still under the 50-min watchdog). Cost: ~+$3-5/mo at trial scope.

experiments.title: grok-4.6 on the funnel + ops surfaces — titles, restock, specials
experiments.baseline: YouTube title bundle, topic-queue restock, and deep-dive specials all on grok-4.3. EN long-form CTR/velocity per the youtube_stats trailing window; restock briefs at the 4.3 depth the queues carry today; the one shipped deep-dive special (spacex q2-2026-earnings) generated on 4.3.
experiments.target: Title bundle: long-form vpd / Shorts velocity on 4.6-era titles at least matches the trailing window (titles are metadata-only — outside landmine 17 — so this can simply run and be read). Restock: next restock cycle's briefs pass validation at the same or better rate. Specials: next forced spacex deep-dive ships on 4.6 with no timeout (specials have no daily-slot pressure).
experiments.criteria: Rollback is per-surface and one line each: the three model defaults in engine/youtube_titles.py; NERRA_RESTOCK_MODEL env or the pin in scripts/restock_topic_queues.py; deep_dive.model in shows/spacex.yaml. Revert a surface if its output quality visibly regresses (title truncation/garbling, restock validation-failure spike, special timeout) — latency canary and envelope guards from the 08-18 outage apply everywhere.
experiments.notes: Wave shipped alongside per-stage model-era stamps (llm_digest_model / llm_script_model in metrics_ep*.json and per-stage model ids in credit files) so every future model question is answerable by query — the credit file's single file-level model label could not represent the trial's split-model episodes. Wave 2 (script-stage pins for omni_view / MAB / MIT + dp_pod comedy-spec re-tightening) is deliberately HELD for the staged-grok-46-trial readout 2026-09-01 per docs/model_upgrade_playbook.md.

experiments.title: Long-form open cliff — hold at the 5% mark
experiments.target: Mean EN audienceWatchRatio at 5% elapsed above 0.55. The curves show ~half the audience gone inside the first 30-45 s while decay flattens after 25% — the open is the dominant remaining retention lever. This entry TRACKS the instrument (new dashboard card + metric); the accelerating open, chapters, and the motion batch are the levers currently in flight against it. Content-side changes to the spoken open are audio (landmine #17) and stay operator-gated.
experiments.notes: Curves accrue nightly for each channel's top 5 recent longs. Outliers worth studying: tesla-RU ep554 held 72% at 5%, spacex ep65 68% — both had thumbnail/title promises the opening delivered immediately.

experiments.title: Late-finishing episodes finally get content-reviewed
experiments.baseline: 4 shows unreviewed on 2026-08-19; a 32-episode network-wide backlog
experiments.target: Zero episodes that finish after the audit window go permanently unreviewed. The backlog drains at <=10/run and stays at 0.
experiments.criteria: Watch the AI-review cost line while the backlog drains — if it spikes, lower CATCH_UP_MAX_PER_RUN rather than dropping the pass.
experiments.notes: Network-wide, not MIT-specific. The first run surfaced real findings that had been invisible, including high cross-episode repetition on MIT Ep139/140.

experiments.title: Modern Investing restarts its track record on published rules
experiments.baseline: holds ran 0-6 sessions (median 3) against a five-day thesis; alpha conflated pick quality with pick weekday
experiments.target: Every weekly hold spans exactly 5 sessions unless stopped out, so per-trade alpha is attributable to the pick. The on-air record is the era only, with its trade count in every sentence, and a listener can reproduce any reported number from the pick date, the symbol and public price data.
experiments.criteria: At readout, score: zero holds off the horizon; zero pre-era figures spoken; confidence ratings actually varying; every pick carrying an invalidation. If holds are still drifting, the exit rule is not being enforced somewhere and that is a bug, not a tuning question.
experiments.notes: The headline alpha goes to zero for about a week and then to a sample too small to claim an edge — that is the intended cost of a reproducible record, and the prompts require the show to say so. Prompt + audio change — landmine #17 A/B.

experiments.title: MIT accounts on air for the record that disappeared
experiments.baseline: Ep141-143 all announced the new era-scoped record; 1 of 3 said why, 0 of 3 pointed at the rulebook or ledger, and 0 of 3 mentioned the +9.28%-across-45-trades figure the show had been quoting.
experiments.target: Exactly 3 episodes carry the correction and then it retires. No listener-value regression below 7.0 on those episodes, and measurable traffic to modern-investing-performance.html within 14 days of the first airing.
experiments.criteria: A 4th airing means the self-retirement is broken. Flat page traffic means the on-air pointer is not working and needs rewording rather than repeating — do NOT extend the run to compensate.
experiments.notes: Deliberately narrow. Pipeline internals are out of scope and a drift guard fails if they leak into the spoken portion. The "published for anyone to check" claim required shipping the performance-page verification panel in the same pass — the ledger was built nightly into api/ and linked from nowhere. First airing was Ep144 (2026-08-20), not Ep145 — the episode shipped after the merge. It exposed two gaps, both fixed: the segment invited verification without naming a destination (so the page-traffic reading would have been meaningless), and it fused with the performance numbers into one paragraph.

experiments.title: Modern Investing trades the options it teaches
experiments.baseline: 0 of 61 simulated trades used an options structure, against options taught in 32 of the last 40 episodes
experiments.target: At least one covered call or cash-secured put per ~10 episodes when the setup genuinely calls for one, each with a real recorded premium and an expiry-settled payoff a listener can reproduce from the underlying's close.
experiments.criteria: Keep if the structures are chosen for the right reason (income on a name worth owning / willingness to own lower) rather than to look sophisticated, and if every position carries a real quote. ANY position recorded with an estimated premium is a revert — that is the whole design constraint. If the show never picks one, the prompt guidance is too weak and needs a nudge, not a mandate.
experiments.notes: Early assignment is not modelled and the prompts require saying so. Audio change — landmine #17 A/B.

experiments.title: Rule scoreboard stops manufacturing verdicts
experiments.baseline: 5 identical RETIREMENT CANDIDATE verdicts from one undivided 10-trade sample, controlled against the disowned pre-era trades
experiments.target: Zero verdicts from collinear rule sets; production-hygiene lessons out of the pick prompt entirely; and a FIRST genuinely scored rule once the era's rule set varies across ~a dozen trades.
experiments.criteria: The loop is allowed to say nothing — that is the fix. What would falsify it is a retirement flag appearing while every stamped trade still carries the same rule set.

experiments.title: Nerra Daily — the combined daily edition
experiments.target: Nonzero OP3 downloads on nerra_daily_podcast.rss by the readout, trending toward the network per-show median. The bet is that a ~2 h all-network edition captures listeners who will not subscribe to 13 feeds.
experiments.criteria: Zero measured downloads at readout (with Apple/Spotify submission done — operator checklist in docs/nerra_daily.md) means the surface is undiscovered, not unwanted: fix distribution before judging the product. Cost is ~$0.08/episode, so the kill bar is low-urgency.
experiments.notes: Audience was UNMEASURED at launch — fetch_op3_stats only walked shows/*.yaml, so the registry-only edition never appeared in api/op3_stats.json (fixed 2026-08-25, same pass that added the edition's cost to the dashboard rollup). First honest read needs a few weeks of post-fix nightly data.

experiments.title: Rule rotation gives the learning loop the variation it needs
experiments.baseline: 2 rule sets across 15 stamped trades, differing by one rule, arising by accident — 0 rules scoreable, ever
experiments.target: >=4 distinct rule sets within 20 era trades, every rule carrying both arms, and at least one genuinely scored rule by ~25 era trades.
experiments.criteria: If 0 rules are scoreable at readout despite the rotation running, the pool (6 rules) is too small and needs widening — not more waiting. If a rule scores well it is pinned automatically and stops rotating, which is the intended end state, not a bug.
experiments.notes: This is an intervention on the product, not just the measurement: some picks are now made without some rules. Proven and hand-pinned rules never rotate out. Rotation is a pure function of the episode number, so any pick's rule set is reproducible from the ledger.

experiments.title: Alpha reported by approach, not only by sector
experiments.baseline: 61 trades, 61 unique free-text strategy strings, 0 groupable
experiments.target: >=90% of new picks carry an explicit family, and at least one family reaches 5 verified-window trades so the show can say on air which approach is actually earning its keep.
experiments.notes: Derived retroactively for the 61 historic trades so the record is groupable now. Inherits the window discipline — indicative-only and not for air until computed over verified windows.

experiments.title: Event specials — earnings/flight reaction episodes
experiments.target: special out-performs the daily episodes around it
experiments.criteria: RESOLVED 2026-08-15 — NEGATIVE. The Q2 special (spacex Ep59) was the WORST RU performer in its neighbourhood by three orders of magnitude (3 RU views vs 2,469 for Ep60) and second-lowest EN long AVP (12.0%), partly because it landed on a 9-upload day (3/day norm). Verdict: specials do not outperform dailies as published; keep them rare, give each its OWN publish day, and enforce the deep-dive brief floor (Ep59 shipped 1775w vs its 2400 floor). Applies to the queued flight-14-catch-reaction special.
experiments.notes: Ep059 (Q2 earnings) is the pilot: compare its 7d views/downloads against Ep057/058/060. flight-14-catch-reaction and q3-2026-earnings are pre-staged in the spacex deep-dive queue.

experiments.title: Staggered Shorts — #1 at publish, rest at channel prime time
experiments.target: RU/EN Short views up WoW with unchanged supply
experiments.criteria: RESOLVED 2026-08-15 — ADOPTED. channel_views_wow_ru +29.7% in the read window with the sweep healthy and zero stranded Shorts. Honesty note: the ru-3-short-band shipped in the same window, so the WoW lift is confounded — adopted on mechanism (scheduler flips reliably, spread confirmed in publish timestamps) rather than on the confounded headline number.
experiments.notes: publishAt scheduling; EN 17/21/23 UTC, RU 15/18/20, FR 17/19/21. First full day 2026-08-07. Confounder note: reads channel views, so a big news day can mask it — check views-per-video too.

experiments.title: RU 3-Short band on spacex + FF
experiments.target: short_vpd holds or grows with 50% more supply
experiments.criteria: RESOLVED 2026-08-15 — POSITIVE. ru_short_vpd_max 60.9 -> 72.5 with 50% more supply: vpd GREW while supply expanded, so the RU audience was not saturated. Band stays; ceiling remains MAX_SHORTS_PER_EPISODE.
experiments.notes: The supply ladder's 20-vpd band. If vpd holds while supply grew, the audience wasn't saturated; if it drops proportionally, it was.

experiments.title: Complete headlines for RU/FR window-Shorts
experiments.target: fragment share of window-Short titles near zero
experiments.criteria: RESOLVED 2026-08-15 — METRIC HIT (0.66 -> 0.10 fragment share). Residual quality defects the metric cannot see (brand garbles: 'Grog 4.6', 'Спейс-Экс', 'Cloud Fable') were fixed separately the same day via restore_brand_names in engine/translate.py. Keep the fragment metric on the dashboard as a regression watch.
experiments.notes: Was ~2/3 of @NerraRU Short titles once the 3-Short band shipped (mid-sentence transcript slices). Grok headline w/ clause-trim fallback; title-only metadata.

experiments.title: Shorts motion A/B — ENDED (operator, 2026-08-14): unreadable
experiments.criteria: RESOLVED 2026-08-14 — operator chose (b): formally ended as unreadable. The treatment arm froze at n=4 when shorts_ab_enabled: false landed via the merged spacex review PR #973; final data (4 vs 12) is not significant and stills remain the network default (no Grok Video spend on Shorts). The four render items the verdict was holding are now shipped on their own merits: progress bar (A3, shipped earlier), Shorts transition split (A2), punch-in easing (E1), long-form closing beat (D2) — all in the scene-cadence-36-slots reading window.
experiments.notes: The A/B machinery (engine/shorts_ab.py, the nightly report) stays dormant and re-usable; kb_extended=False keeps reproducing the legacy control render if a future experiment wants it.

experiments.title: Cold open — hook is the first thing spoken
experiments.target: long-form median AVP off the ~11% floor
experiments.criteria: RESOLVED 2026-08-15 — POSITIVE. long_form_median_avp_en_14d 11.3 -> 13.4 (+2.1pp, ~19% relative). The cold open stays; no revert. Long-form retention remains far below Shorts (~72-77%), so the next retention lever is content-shape, not the intro.
experiments.notes: Ten seconds of theme + a 35-word greeting used to push the first fact to ~second 28; Shorts (which skip the intro) hold ~42% on the same audio. Audio change — was A/B-listened per landmine #17.

experiments.title: Network-wide grok-4.6 — all LLM stages off 4.3 (operator-directed)
experiments.baseline: grok-4.3 on digest/fetch/scripts/synth/titles/reviewer; 30d LLM token spend ~$25 (would be ~$47 at 4.6 rates on the same tokens); script under-floor share 81% network-wide (MIT 9/10 under 1800w); episode-reviewer FACTUAL_ERRORS flags at the pre-upgrade rate (establish from review_report history at readout).
experiments.target: Script length off the 4.3 plateau (MIT median clears 1700w+; the chronically-short shows' under-floor share drops), reviewer FACTUAL_ERRORS flag rate NOT above the pre-upgrade baseline, and refusal-fallback fires stay rare. LLM cost line lands ~$45-50/30d.
experiments.criteria: OPERATOR OVERRIDE of the July-31 digests-stay-on-4.3 decision (explicitly directed 2026-08-18, risks acknowledged: 4.6's confident-hallucination profile is unmeasured for this network). REVERT TRIGGERS, checked daily via the audit, decided at readout: (1) any invented number/ticker/price in an MIT script — immediate one-line revert (model: grok-4.3 in _defaults.yaml); (2) reviewer FACTUAL_ERRORS rate clearly above baseline across shows; (3) fetch tool-calls (x_search/web_search) failing on 4.6. Also A/B-listen the first post-merge episode on 2-3 shows per landmine #17 — every script's prose changes with this merge.
experiments.notes: Everything moved together: digest/fetch, scripts (dp_pod's 4.5 and MIT's 4.6 pins removed — superseded/absorbed), synth, titles, reviewer, review agent, restock; refusal fallback repointed grok-4.20-reasoning -> grok-4.3 (different snapshot than the new primary, retires the aging 4.20 dependency). Translation was already pinned 4.6 same-day. ~+$22-25/mo at current volume. REVERTED SAME DAY (2026-08-18, operator-directed): the trigger was OPERATIONAL, not on the registered list — 4.6 digest latency ran 5-10x 4.3 on every show measured (planetterrian 44s -> 420s, MAB 36s -> 242s, dp_pod 55s -> 225s, first_principles 36s -> 205s) and on the four largest digest prompts (tesla, spacex, omni_view, modern_investing) requests exceeded the 300s client timeout or were server-disconnected. Nested SDK+tenacity retries amplified each stall into a 41-45 min burn; 7 of 12 shows failed on day one (2026-08-18 07:37-10:33 UTC). Rolled back to grok-4.3 everywhere except the translation pin (already 4.6 via the alias freeze, small chunks, no timeouts observed). The hallucination-profile question is UNANSWERED — the experiment never reached an editorial readout. Any retry follows docs/model_upgrade_playbook.md: one show first, digest-latency gate before network-wide.

experiments.title: RU+FR long-form dubs on tesla / spacex / FF (operator override)
experiments.target: RU/FR long_vpd clearing the RU floor (2.0) with retention above the ~9% the July demotion measured; watch fr_long_vpd_max too.
experiments.criteria: RESOLVED 2026-08-15 — NEGATIVE, ended 6 days early per the experiment's own exit rule: ru_long_vpd 1.52 vs the 2.0 floor, 52 forced RU/FR longs earned 461 total views (~9/video) and a net -2 subscribers — the July demotion numbers repeated almost exactly. dub_force_long_channels removed from tesla/spacex/FF; the adaptive policy's shorts-only tier decides again. Do not re-probe without a materially different format (e.g. native-RU presentation rather than a dubbed EN render).
experiments.notes: Operator-directed: dub_force_long_channels pins long-form ON for the big three on both dub channels regardless of tier; the Shorts supply ladder is untouched. Overrides the July RU long demotion (~9% retention, ~11 views/video) to give dubbed long-form a second, deliberate read. If the readout repeats the July numbers, remove the YAML flags and let the policy decide again.

experiments.title: DP Pod script stage on grok-4.5 — SUPERSEDED by network 4.6 upgrade
experiments.baseline: 27/30 episodes with zero exclamation points; ~30% median digest-to-script 10-word shingle overlap (Ep22 65%)
experiments.target: Scripts stop reading the brief verbatim (<=15% median shingle overlap) and the delivery spec finally lands (>=2 exclamation points in most episodes, voice tags actually used) with NO new facts beyond the digest.
experiments.criteria: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-18 — the operator-directed network-wide grok-4.6 upgrade moved dp_pod's script stage (and every other stage) to 4.6, ending the 4.5 arm early. The 08-10..08-18 4.5 episodes are still a usable partial read: score the shingle-overlap/exclamation ledger predictions against them at the original 08-24 date, then judge 4.6 under network-grok-46-upgrade.
experiments.notes: Was the first show on the July-31 script-stage model knob. Audio change — landmine #17 A/B applied at ship time.

experiments.title: Modern Investing script stage on grok-4.6 — ABSORBED into network 4.6 upgrade
experiments.baseline: median script 1535w against an 1800w floor; 9 of the last 10 episodes below it
experiments.target: Median script length reaches the 1800w floor (or at least clears 1700w) with NO facts, tickers, prices or performance figures beyond what the digest carries. Length has been attacked at the digest substrate since July 24 and moved only 1382w -> 1535w, which points at the script stage as the remaining ceiling.
experiments.criteria: ABSORBED 2026-08-18 into the operator-directed network-wide 4.6 upgrade (the explicit podcast_model pin was removed — the network default now equals what this A/B was trialling, and the digest moved too, so the script-vs-digest isolation this experiment relied on no longer exists). At 08-29 still score the length target (median script vs the 1800w floor) from the 08-15+ episodes; the factuality check transfers to network-grok-46-upgrade, where MIT remains the revert trigger.
experiments.notes: Ran 3 days as a script-stage-only A/B before the network upgrade landed. The MIT rule carries forward unchanged: any invented number/ticker/price reaching a script is an immediate revert.
